title: Warren presses Lutnick over UAE access to sensitive U.S. tech after Trump crypto investment
headline_summary: Warren questions Lutnick over UAE tech access, Trump crypto investment
blurb: Warren pressed Commerce Secretary Lutnick on export control decisions tied to UAE investment in Trump's crypto venture. The administration eased restrictions on sensitive technology access to UAE entities while they simultaneously invested in the venture. This episode signals intensifying regulatory risk for crypto startups attracting foreign capital and geopolitical factors embedded in U.S. venture funding.

title: FCA moves to simplify UK IPO listing rules
headline_summary: FCA removes research delays to streamline UK IPO listings
blurb: The FCA removed the mandatory seven-day waiting period for connected analyst research following publication of an approved IPO prospectus or registration document, eliminating a material procedural delay that previously constrained listing timelines. This Financial Conduct Authority reform streamlines the UK's public listing process for VC-backed companies and improves the efficiency of syndicate operations. Faster IPO timelines reduce exit friction for founders, strengthen capital efficiency metrics that LPs track, and position the UK as a more competitive public markets destination.

title: SEC and CFTC advance Project Crypto as fallback to the Clarity Act
headline_summary: SEC and CFTC advance Project Crypto regulatory framework
blurb: The SEC and CFTC are advancing Project Crypto as a coordinated regulatory framework, designed as a direct contingency if comprehensive crypto legislation stalls in Congress. The agencies are jointly developing rules on digital asset custody, exchange standards, and regulatory jurisdiction. Agency-driven clarity removes compliance ambiguity that's blocked institutional capital flows into crypto ventures and provides builders with predictable operating rules.

title: Yann LeCun joins new $100M AI fund, weeks after his last one lasted 8 hours
headline_summary: Yann LeCun joins 224 Ventures' new $100M AI fund
blurb: Yann LeCun has joined 224 Ventures as it launches a new $100M AI fund. The former Meta chief AI scientist makes the move just weeks after his previous fund attempt collapsed within 8 hours, an unusual stumble for a deep learning pioneer. The rapid reboot demonstrates venture capital's continued appetite for elite technical founders regardless of recent setbacks.

title: [AINews] Jeff, Sanjay, Oriol, and Quoc depart DeepMind; Demis to Chair; Koray to SVP — what is going on at GDM???
headline_summary: Four DeepMind researchers depart; Demis chairs, Koray to SVP
blurb: Four senior DeepMind researchers depart: Jeff Dean, Sanjay Agarwal, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le. Demis Hassabis shifts to chair while Koray Bourou takes SVP role. This significant restructuring at Google's flagship AI research lab signals either a major strategic redirection or meaningful brain drain toward competing research labs, startups, and independent teams—critical for VCs tracking where top-tier AI talent flows next.

title: Google reveals big shakeup in its AI teams as Jeff Dean leaves and Demis Hassabis moves upstairs
headline_summary: Demis Hassabis elevated to Alphabet Chief Scientist as Jeff Dean exits
blurb: Alphabet promoted Demis Hassabis from Google Deepmind CEO to Alphabet Chief Scientist and Chairman. Jeff Dean, Google's Chief Scientist for 27 years, is departing. The reshuffle consolidates AI strategy under Hassabis and signals Deepmind's elevation as the conglomerate's primary AI engine—a major organizational shift that clarifies capital allocation, product roadmap authority, and Alphabet's strategic priorities for competing in AGI.

title: Google's AI shake-up: DeepMind's Hassabis steps aside, senior scientists depart
headline_summary: DeepMind chief Hassabis exits Google, AI talent exodus continues
blurb: Demis Hassabis, DeepMind's founder and CEO, is stepping down as Google reshapes its AI research division. Multiple senior scientists are departing the lab in what marks the latest wave of high-profile exits from DeepMind. For VCs tracking talent flows and founder recruiting pipelines, this signals where top AI researchers go next and which well-funded startups can recruit them.

title: Google Overhauls AI Leadership as Longtime Chief Scientist Joins Wave of Exits
headline_summary: Jeff Dean launches AI startup; Hassabis takes DeepMind helm
blurb: Jeff Dean is exiting Google to launch an AI-discovery startup while Demis Hassabis assumes chairmanship of Google DeepMind. Dean has been one of Google's most prolific and influential AI researchers. This reflects a broader trend of top-tier AI talent exiting big tech to found startups—a critical signal for VCs tracking which founders and new AI ventures will emerge next.

title: The startup idea that convinced a UW computer science legend to leave Google after 27 years
headline_summary: Google legend Jeff Dean leaves to found AI research automation startup
blurb: Jeff Dean, Google's legendary computer scientist and University of Washington Ph.D., is leaving the company after 27 years to found Discovery Loop with three of Google's top AI researchers. Google is backing the venture as an investor. The departure concentrates senior AI talent in scientific automation—a frontier generating significant venture capital interest and raising questions about talent retention within Google's elite AI research organization.

title: Yann LeCun joins new VC firm
headline_summary: Yann LeCun joins new VC firm backed by 244 LPs
blurb: Yann LeCun, Meta's chief AI scientist, joins a newly-formed venture capital firm as a founding partner. The firm secured backing from 244 institutional LPs, representing significant firepower in the AI-first investment space. LeCun's appointment signals major capital consolidating around deep-tech and AI infrastructure—a key read for founders building research-backed startups.

title: Lumilens, which is building data center optical-interconnection tech to replace wires with light, raised $700M at a $5.5B valuation, for $900M in total funding (Anissa Gardizy/Wall Street Journal)
headline_summary: Lumilens raises $700M for optical data center interconnection tech
blurb: Lumilens just closed a $700M funding round at $5.5B valuation, bringing total capital to $900M. The company manufactures optical-interconnection hardware replacing copper cables in data centers, substantially improving data transfer between AI compute clusters. The investment signals growing investor confidence that optical interconnection infrastructure is essential for scaling AI—and captures defensible value in an increasingly critical, competitive infrastructure layer.

title: SpaceX stock could face further pressure as first batch of shares unlock since IPO
headline_summary: SpaceX stock faces pressure as first insider shares unlock post-IPO
blurb: SpaceX's initial post-IPO lockup period expires, allowing founders, early investors, and company executives to sell their shares. The first tranche of insider stock enters the public markets simultaneously. This unlock tests the IPO's valuation stability and reveals genuine market appetite for mega-cap exits—critical indicators for venture investors assessing the true post-IPO value of similar companies approaching their public market debuts.

title: SoftBank reports Q1 net profit down 18% YoY to ~$2.2B, above ~$761M est., an ~$8.2B gain on its Intel stake, and Vision Fund up $1.7B due to its ByteDance stake (Arjun Kharpal/CNBC)
headline_summary: SoftBank Q1 profit beats estimates on $8.2B Intel, $1.7B Vision gains
blurb: SoftBank reported Q1 net profit of $2.2B, beating analyst estimates despite an 18% year-over-year decline. Results were driven by an $8.2B gain on its Intel stake and $1.7B rise in Vision Fund value from ByteDance holdings. This snapshot of mega-cap technology valuations and portfolio concentration signals how the venture industry's largest capital allocator is currently positioned.

title: NFT startup founder charged with misusing funds from $10 million fundraising
headline_summary: NFT founder charged with misusing $10M fundraise
blurb: An NFT startup founder faces criminal charges for misusing $10 million in investor capital from a fundraising round. The allegations target a key founder in the cryptocurrency space. Venture investors with significant exposure to the crypto sector now face harder due-diligence questions around founder integrity and capital controls, as governance gaps emerge as tangible portfolio risks.

title: European AI funding hit $23B in H1 2026 but the US raised 14 times more
headline_summary: European AI funding hits $23B in H1 but trails US by 14x
blurb: European AI startups raised $23 billion in H1 2026, up 130% from the prior year. US investors allocated roughly $322 billion, or 14 times more capital, cementing decisively higher concentration. For VCs and LPs, the data signals European AI's accelerating growth but highlights why US-backed founders maintain structural advantages: deeper capital pools, faster deployment cycles, and historically higher exit multiples on scale.

title: Germany’s newest unicorn: Moss bags €30M to hit €1B valuation, aims for profitability by 2027
headline_summary: Berlin startup Moss hits €1B valuation with €30M raise
blurb: Moss, a Berlin startup, raised €30M to achieve €1B valuation and become Germany's newest unicorn. The company was founded by four entrepreneurs who identified and solved operational challenges at their previous company before launching their own venture. The funding round signals continued investor appetite for German startups that have demonstrated unit economics and a clear path to profitability by 2027.

title: Circle Names BlackRock, Visa, ICE and DTCC Among 11 Founding Arc Validators
headline_summary: Circle launches Arc with BlackRock, Visa, ICE validators
blurb: Circle announces Arc, a permissioned blockchain network with 11 founding validators: BlackRock, Visa, ICE, DTCC, and seven others. These institutional validators will directly operate the network, representing a credibility signal for crypto infrastructure. The move bypasses regulatory review—Arc is not examined by the SEC or NYDFS—but signals institutional finance advancing blockchain infrastructure independently without waiting for regulatory clarity.

title: ‘Nobody Wanted to Give A Former Principal Money’: How An Educator Built An Edtech AI Startup With $63M From VCs
headline_summary: Educator-founded MagicSchool AI raises $63M in VC funding
blurb: MagicSchool AI raised $63M in VC funding this year. The education startup was founded by a former principal applying ChatGPT to schools; the founder initially struggled to raise capital because investors doubted backing a non-technical educator. The funding signals a major shift: VCs now aggressively invest in AI/edtech and see education as a primary sector for non-traditional founder backing and AI deployment.

title: SpaceX Stock Falls 7% as Capital Spending Hits $18.4 Billion in Debut Quarter
headline_summary: SpaceX falls 7% as capital spending hits $18.4 billion
blurb: SpaceX's stock fell 7% after the company disclosed $18.4 billion in capital spending for its first post-IPO quarter—six times the prior year. Satellite connectivity was the only profitable segment. The capex intensity underscores why space infrastructure requires sustained capital investment even at the public company scale—essential context for VCs modeling the long-term financial requirements of competing deeptech ventures.

title: After a decade of turning down VCs, Oxylabs hits $3.6bn valuation: 'Right timing, right partner'
headline_summary: Oxylabs reaches $3.6bn after decade rejecting VC
blurb: Oxylabs, a web scraping and data intelligence platform, reached a $3.6bn valuation in a major milestone for the enterprise data infrastructure category. The Lithuania-based company rejected outside VC funding for more than a decade before recently reversing course and accepting capital. The shift signals strong market appetite for data services and underscores founder confidence that external investment drives meaningful growth without compromising independence.

title: The 144 new funds this year and what they reveal about Europe's investment market
headline_summary: 144 new European funds reveal market consolidation pressures
blurb: Europe saw 144 new fund launches this year, a significant inflection point in the continent's investment landscape. The surge signals meaningful shifts in LP capital allocation patterns and renewed interest in emerging geographies, fund types, and specialized managers. For VCs and founders, it indicates both a more diverse capital ecosystem and significantly more competitive dynamics for fund formation and capital deployment opportunities.

title: SpaceX, in First Earnings After IPO, Reports Soaring AI Spending
headline_summary: SpaceX's first earnings show seven-fold capex surge on AI
blurb: SpaceX reported its first post-IPO earnings showing capital expenditures surged sevenfold year-over-year. AI spending jumped sharply alongside strong revenue growth, representing a major shift in where the company deploys resources. For VCs tracking capex trends and aerospace competition, the spending scale signals how aggressively SpaceX is investing in AI infrastructure and how the company's strategy is evolving as a public entity.

title: Oxide Computer raises $445M (SEC Form D)
headline_summary: Oxide Computer closes $445M funding round for ARM servers
blurb: Oxide Computer closed a $445M private funding round, formally disclosed via SEC Form D filing. The startup manufactures custom ARM-based server platforms for cloud operators and enterprises seeking alternatives to conventional x86-based architectures. This substantial capital raise reflects sustained LP conviction in compute infrastructure and demonstrates persistent investor appetite for custom silicon strategies outside the increasingly crowded AI hardware sector.

title: A16z backs HappyRobot at $1.2bn valuation
headline_summary: A16z backs HappyRobot at $1.2bn valuation
blurb: A16z invested in HappyRobot at a $1.2bn valuation, marking a significant growth-stage investment decision. A16z, one of the world's largest venture firms, continues aggressively deploying capital at this scale, reflecting sustained appetite from tier-one VCs. The deal signals strong market momentum for founders seeking growth capital and validates that venture capital flows readily to well-positioned teams with proven execution track records.

title: Monava closes funding round as demand for passive drone detection grows
headline_summary: Monava closes defencetech funding for acoustic drone detection
blurb: Monava closed a funding round led by Gungnir Capital, with participation from Foundry Ventures and Hede. The Swedish-Finnish defencetech startup specializes in acoustic drone detection, enabling unmanned aircraft identification without active radar systems. The capital raise reflects accelerating market demand for passive detection infrastructure solutions as commercial and military drone deployments expand globally, indicating a maturing ecosystem for air-defense technology.

title: Multi-day energy storage startup Ore Energy clinches $43M in new investment round
headline_summary: Ore Energy lands $43M Series A for multi-day battery tech
blurb: Ore Energy closed a $43M Series A round led by new investors to commercialize long-duration battery technology for power grids. The Dutch startup develops multi-day energy storage systems for grid-scale applications. Extended-duration storage fills a critical infrastructure gap: as renewable energy grows, grids need batteries holding power for days rather than hours to maximize dispatch flexibility and avoid costly overbuilding.

title: European robotics startups raised more in six months than past two years combined
headline_summary: European robotics funding surges past two-year total in six months
blurb: European robotics startups raised more capital in the last six months than the entire prior two years combined—a sharp inflection. The surge reflects strong LP commitments and renewed VC appetite for hardware and automation. This matters for capital allocators because it signals Europe is now competitive for deeptech robotics funding after years of underinvestment versus Asia.

title: Active Crypto VC Firms Fall to 150, Lowest Since 2020
headline_summary: Active crypto VC firms fall to 150, lowest since 2020
blurb: Active crypto venture firms have collapsed to 150, the lowest count since 2020. CryptoRank tracked 1,177 unique investors at the March 2022 peak; today's number represents an 87% decline in the active venture investor base. This consolidation signals a much tougher funding environment for early-stage crypto projects, with fewer players controlling capital allocation and higher due diligence standards becoming standard practice.

title: China Closes the Satellite Gap in Space Race With the US
headline_summary: China narrows satellite capability gap with US in space competition
blurb: China is closing the satellite technology gap with the US, demonstrating accelerated progress in space infrastructure and launch capabilities. This advancement reflects sustained Chinese investment and rapid development of advanced orbital systems over recent years. For VCs in deeptech and commercial space investment, this signals intensifying global competition in satellite and launch markets, fundamentally reshaping investment theses for space-backed startups and infrastructure companies.

title: Leopold Aschenbrenner’s AI fund lost most of its value. Now it’s back with $400M.
headline_summary: AI fund Situational Awareness returns with $400M after July collapse
blurb: Situational Awareness, the AI fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, nearly imploded in July, losing roughly two-thirds of its total value in what threatened to be a catastrophic failure. The firm has now returned to investing with a $400M capital commitment. The swift recovery signals strong backer confidence and demonstrates sustained investor appetite for high-conviction AI bets despite the recent market volatility.

title: UAE Fund Weighs $6.3 Billion AI Data Center Investment in Japan
headline_summary: UAE fund weighs $6.3B AI data center investment in Japan
blurb: A UAE fund is evaluating a $6.3 billion investment to build advanced AI data center infrastructure in Japan. The ¥1 trillion commitment signals significant capital flowing into foundational AI infrastructure outside the United States market. For venture investors tracking infrastructure consolidation and geopolitical capital flows, this shows that sovereign wealth funds and state actors now compete directly with US tech companies for critical compute capacity.

title: Defense tech company Hadrian raised a $1.37B Series D at an $8B valuation to expand its factories and Opus software platform, after a $260M Series C in 2025 (Colin Demarest/Axios)
headline_summary: Hadrian raises $1.37B Series D at $8B valuation for defense expansion
blurb: Hadrian, a defense manufacturer and factory builder, raised $1.37 billion in Series D at an $8 billion valuation. The capital funds expansion of its Opus software platform and manufacturing capacity, accelerating growth from a $260 million Series C round in 2025. The raise signals strong venture investor appetite for defense-critical hardware infrastructure and supply chain resilience solutions amid current geopolitical tensions.

title: Sequoia doubles down on AI with $10B fund under new leadership
headline_summary: Sequoia launches $10B AI fund under new leadership
blurb: Sequoia raised a $10 billion fund dedicated to AI startups. Alfred Lin led the push after his partners rejected a $1 billion Anthropic allocation as undersized. The fund, launched under new leadership, reflects Sequoia's conviction that AI dominance requires concentrated capital. For the venture market, it signals that category leadership now demands first-mover capital concentration in platform shifts.

title: A look at Sequoia's revamped strategy under new stewards Alfred Lin and Pat Grady, including bold AI bets; sources: Sequoia recently closed $10B in new funding (Bloomberg)
headline_summary: Sequoia closes $10B, pivots strategy under Lin and Grady toward AI
blurb: Sequoia Capital closed a $10B fund and repositioned under new leadership. Alfred Lin and Pat Grady now lead the 54-year-old firm's strategic pivot to make artificial intelligence its core investment focus for the foreseeable future. This generational change signals strong LP confidence in concentrated AI-heavy portfolios and marks a major leadership transition at one of venture capital's most influential and largest firms.

title: Robinhood to list a fund that lets anyone back Y Combinator startups
headline_summary: Robinhood launches retail fund for Y Combinator startups
blurb: Robinhood is launching a fund that allows retail investors to back Y Combinator startups. The brokerage's new financial instrument democratizes access to early-stage venture deals historically limited to accredited investors and institutional LPs. For VCs and founders, this signals growing pressure to open cap tables to retail investors and demonstrates sustained retail appetite for startup exposure beyond traditional public markets.

title: White Star Capital closes $250M Fund IV to back global startups from Series A to B
headline_summary: White Star Capital closes $250M Fund IV for Series A-B startups
blurb: White Star Capital announced the final close of Fund IV at $250 million, targeting global startups in Series A-to-B rounds. The firm now operates alongside its North American Seed Fund, announced late last year, extending its reach across geographies and investment stages. Fund closes of this size from established VCs signal LP confidence and active capital deployment in venture markets.

title: Scaleup Europe Fund makes debut investment by co-leading ICEYE’s €1 billion Series F round
headline_summary: Scaleup Europe Fund debuts with €450M co-lead in ICEYE's €1B Series F
blurb: Scaleup Europe Fund, EQT's new deep-tech investment vehicle, made its debut investment by co-leading ICEYE's €1 billion Series F round. The SpaceTech round raised €450 million in primary capital, valuing the Finnish startup well above €10 billion. A new fund's first check signals where European institutional capital is flowing and reflects LP confidence in frontier space hardware operating at scale.

title: Tempo plans to support BlackRock's new money market fund
headline_summary: Tempo to support BlackRock's new money market fund
blurb: BlackRock is launching a new money market fund with infrastructure support from Tempo. The partnership reflects a major $10T+ asset manager adopting digital asset infrastructure, validating years of fintech infrastructure investment. For VC readers tracking institutional capital flows into crypto platforms, this move by BlackRock demonstrates institutional demand for digital asset infrastructure and will accelerate capital flows into fintech platforms.

title: How Mechanize went from a $9M seed to $1.5B Google acquisition talks in just 100 days
headline_summary: Mechanize: $9M seed to $1.5B Google talks in 100 days
blurb: Mechanize closed a $9.1M seed round in April 2026 and reached $1.5B acquisition talks with Google within 100 days. The 46-person startup accelerated from newly funded status to acquisition target far faster than typical venture timelines would allow for such scaling. For VCs tracking M&A patterns, this demonstrates how major acquirers are now actively and aggressively competing for early-stage teams with strong founder execution.

title: Filing: Hangzhou-based Unitree Robotics prices its Shanghai IPO at ~$22/share, aiming to sell 40.4M shares to raise $904M; Unitree shipped 5,500+ robots in 2025 (Bloomberg)
headline_summary: Unitree Robotics prices Shanghai IPO at $22/share, raises $904M
blurb: Unitree Robotics prices its Shanghai IPO at approximately $22 per share, targeting $904 million in gross proceeds from 40.4 million shares offered publicly. The Hangzhou-based robotics company shipped over 5,500 quadruped and humanoid units throughout 2025, demonstrating significant production scale and durable commercial market traction. For venture capital investors, the exit signals strong institutional appetite for hardware automation platforms and validates the investment thesis that robotics commercialization is maturing from speculative venture bets into a durable, increasingly capital-intensive and commercially viable asset class.

title: China’s Unitree Seeks $904 Million in First Mainland Robotic IPO
headline_summary: Unitree Robotics targets $904M IPO, China's first robot maker
blurb: Yushu Technology, trading as Unitree Robotics, is raising $904 million through an IPO on mainland Chinese exchanges. The humanoid robotics company would become the first of its kind to go public in mainland China, signaling the sector's maturation. For VCs, this signals investor appetite for high-capex robotics hardware and validates China's push to compete with US-based robotics leaders.

title: Chinese launch startup Orienspace targets IPO, secures funding for reusable Gravity-2 rocket
headline_summary: Orienspace targets IPO, raises funding for reusable Gravity-2 rocket
blurb: Orienspace, a Chinese commercial launch startup, is preparing for an IPO and closing a new funding round for its Gravity-2 reusable rocket. The Shandong-based company is pursuing simultaneous capital raise and public-market entry to accelerate rocket development and production. For VCs tracking space, this signals a major rival consolidating capital and matching Western reusable-launch capabilities—reshaping competition in commercial spaceflight.

title: Alibaba-Backed AI Startup Vast Seeks Fresh Capital, Eyes IPO
headline_summary: Alibaba-backed AI unicorn Vast pursues capital, targets IPO
blurb: Vast, an Alibaba and Baidu-backed artificial-intelligence unicorn, is in active talks to raise fresh capital, with an IPO reportedly on the horizon. The Chinese startup has achieved unicorn status, backed by two of Asia's largest technology firms. This signals China's AI infrastructure sector is maturing rapidly, with late-stage investors actively positioning portfolio companies for near-term public-market exits.

title: Airtable Just Sold for $2.25B at 2.7x ARR. It Raised $1.4B and Was Once Worth $11.7B. This Was … Market
headline_summary: Airtable sells to Bending Spoons for $2.25B, down from $11.7B peak
blurb: Bending Spoons is acquiring Airtable in an all-cash deal for approximately $2.25B enterprise value, expected to close by year-end. The no-code database platform reported $480M ARR as of June 2026, growing over 20% year-over-year with roughly 90% gross margins. The transaction represents a steep valuation reset from Airtable's prior $11.7B peak and signals where late-stage SaaS exits are pricing in the current market.

title: Saudi wealth fund and Jared Kushner's Affinity finalize $55 billion EA Sports deal
headline_summary: PIF and Affinity finalize $55B EA Sports acquisition, delist from Nasdaq
blurb: Affinity Partners and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund are taking EA Sports private in a $55 billion deal at $210 per share. Nasdaq delisting is effective today. The acquisition signals where sovereign wealth deploys capital in entertainment and establishes Affinity as a major operator anchoring transformational deals—a proxy for how institutional capital is clustering in this cycle.

title: Nik Storonsky in talks over new share deal for $500bn Revolut valuation
headline_summary: Nik Storonsky in talks on $500B Revolut secondary deal
blurb: Revolut founder Nik Storonsky is negotiating a secondary share deal or new funding round at a $500 billion valuation. The London-based fintech giant is one of Europe's most valuable private companies. Secondary deals at this scale typically signal major investor confidence and often precede IPO announcements or acquisition, making this a crucial data point for venture funds tracking fintech exits.

title: Visa to Buy BioCatch for $2.4 Billion, Nearly Double Its 2024 Valuation
headline_summary: Visa buys fraud-detection startup BioCatch for $2.4 billion
blurb: Visa is acquiring BioCatch for $2.4 billion in cash. The Tel Aviv behavioral biometrics firm uses typing speed, mouse patterns, and device-handling analysis to detect fraud across 760 million users worldwide; this deal nearly doubles BioCatch's valuation from its 2024 level under Permira's former majority ownership. Behavioral authentication is now core infrastructure for payment networks competing on fraud detection and risk mitigation.

title: Bending Spoons strikes $2.25bn Airtable deal in first acquisition since IPO
headline_summary: Bending Spoons acquires Airtable for $2.25B, first post-IPO deal
blurb: Bending Spoons acquired no-code platform Airtable for $2.25 billion. The Italian software consolidator's first major post-IPO acquisition signals confidence in consolidating profitable SaaS businesses at scale. The deal validates Airtable's market position and demonstrates that public tech companies will pay substantial multiples for founder-led, capital-efficient platforms—a significant signal for exit valuations in the no-code and low-code infrastructure space.
